objective: Identify key indicators of customer attrition, build predictive models to estimate churn probability, and propose data-driven retention strategies.

methodology.description: Handled missing values in Total_Charges, converted data types, and encoded categorical variables using One-Hot Encoding.
Analyzed churn distribution across contract types, payment methods, and tenure bands. Discovered higher churn in month-to-month contracts and fiber optic users.
Created features such as Average_Monthly_Spend, Support_Ticket_Frequency, and Tenure_Group.
Trained Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost classifiers. Evaluated performance using ROC-AUC, Recall, and Precision.
Formulated targeted retention campaigns for high-risk customers, prioritizing users with tenure < 12 months and high ticket counts.

key_findings: Month-to-month contract holders are 4x more likely to churn compared to two-year contract holders.
Customers with more than 3 customer service calls within 6 months showed an 82% churn probability.
Opting for automatic payment methods reduced churn rates by 28%.
